g.text: Two samples with the same mean
Both samples have a mean of 20, but Sample 1 runs from 10 to 30
Plotting the individual values shows the wider spread in Sample 1
Equal means do not mean identical observations.
Population density of regions A and B
A (20 per km²) is in the highest class: 20 is the lower limit of
“20 or more”, so it cannot be in “10 to under 20”.
B (10 per km²) is in the middle class, “10 to under 20”: the
boundary value goes up, so each value has one class.
Each shade is an average for the whole region; it does not show
whether people are spread evenly inside A or B.

It is an estimate, not an extra observation. If values change
unevenly (dashed curve), the real crossing could lie elsewhere,
and nothing is known beyond the segment.
